To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the choice of the unstructured contact component in individual-based models can affect the evaluation of the effectiveness in containing/mitigating an epidemic.
different modeling choices can lead to a different assessment of the effectiveness of intervention measures.

the unstructured contacts component in influenza pandemic models can have a significant effect on the model output and on the evaluation of the effectiveness and the impact of intervention strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the impact of different modeling approaches to unstructured contacts on the epidemic spread?

improving the modeling of the unstructured component in individual based models, in order to better predict the spatiotemporally dynamics of epidemics and evaluate the effectiveness of mitigation/containment strategies.
a better understanding of the role of the unstructured component of contacts in the spread of the influenza pandemic and the evaluation of its impact on the model outputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a model-based evaluation of intervention strategies for influenza pandemics requires not only a careful choice of model parameters and a detailed description of the intervention strategy, but also a thorough sensitivity analysis with respect to different choices of model structure.

, while the choice of the model is important for understanding the impact of interventions and for evaluating the potential risk of an outbreak, the choice of the data to inform the model is equally important.
, for the considered model, a more realistic description of the unstructured contact component leads to a more optimistic scenario, in terms of both attack rate and peak day.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of a model for a given epidemic is not only a question of data availability but also a question of policy making and of the desired outcomes of the model.

, in order to reduce uncertainty in the model outputs, data on contacts in neglected environments and time-use data should be employed and the possible effects of various modeling assumptions should be considered.
the unstructured contacts component is a key factor in influenza pandemic modeling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the choice of unstructured contacts has a significant impact on model results, it can be reduced by employing available data.

the impact of unstructured contacts on the spread of the pandemic should be considered in any model and that it should be carefully evaluated in order to avoid over- or under-estimation of the epidemic spread and of the effectiveness of containment/mitigation strategies.
the choice of the unstructured contact model is crucial to obtain reliable results and thus to take public health decisions.
